name: returns
title: Returns
summary: Return policies (platform baseline, seller terms, category exceptions, who pays return shipping), per-item eligibility, return requests and decisions, return shipments, receipt and inspection, remedies (refund, replacement, exchange) and the refund request that Finance approves before payments sends the money.
owns: Platform return baseline with versions and effective dates, category exceptions and the who-pays-return-shipping matrix
Seller return terms (more generous than the baseline, never less) and the effective terms resolved for an offer
Eligibility check per item and quantity before submission: deadline, destination, shipping responsibility, remedy options, refund estimate
Return requests (RT- references) by item and quantity with reason, details and photos; one return per seller
Seller and platform decisions: approve, request information, reject with explanation, published response deadlines
Platform intervention when a seller misses a deadline or the customer challenges an outcome
Return shipments tracked separately from the original delivery: prepaid label or QR drop-off, customer-arranged tracking
Receipt, inspection (condition outcome, grade, missing parts, photos) and the proposed stock outcome
Remedies: full or partial refund with an itemised breakdown, replacement or exchange with its own shipment, store credit when the wallet module is on
Refund requests (Requested, Under review, Approved, Declined) and their mirrored payment progress (Processing, Sent, Failed)
Refund-without-return as a controlled exception with a recorded reason
notOwns: Sending money and refund retries: payments (returns hands over an approved refund and mirrors its status)
Seller earnings, fee refunds and post-payout deductions: finance (reads returns.refund.approved and payments.refund.sent)
Carrier labels, rates and tracking feeds: shipping (returns asks shipping for a return label and listens for tracking events)
Stock movements for returned units: inventory (returns proposes the stock outcome; inventory records it)
Customer/seller disputes, decisions and appeals: support (a return links to its dispute case)
Customer-facing policy pages: content (returns supplies the policy data shown on them)

stateMachines.name: Return
stateMachines.notes: Customer labels: requested→Requested, info_requested→Waiting for you, approved→Approved (send it back), in_transit→Sent back, received→Received, awaiting_remedy→Inspected (or Approved without return), completed→Refunded / Replaced / Partly refunded, rejected→Rejected, cancelled→Cancelled. Seller labels: Return requested, Waiting on customer, Return in transit, Inspecting, Escalated (platformHandling flag), Decision made. The respond-by clock pauses while info_requested. approveWithoutReturn / waiveReturn require a recorded reason (refund-without-return exception). overturn is a platform action (returns.returns.manage) after a customer challenges a seller rejection. complete fires automatically when the remedy finishes: refund Sent, replacement shipped, or store credit issued.

stateMachines.name: Return shipment
stateMachines.notes: Driven by shipping tracking events for the return label (first carrier scan = dropOff). Customer-arranged returns start at label_issued without a label and move to in_transit when the customer adds tracking (returns registers it with shipping.registerReturnTracking so carrier events arrive like any return parcel). A label activates when the carrier scans the QR code. Lost in transit to the warehouse leads to waiveReturn on the return with a carrier claim.

stateMachines.name: Refund request
stateMachines.notes: Plan ch. 13 refund statuses. requested = estimate shown at request time. Seller-issued refunds for the seller's own return go requested→approved (the seller is the approver). Official Store, platform-decided, case and exception refunds go through under_review and Finance approval (returns.refunds.approve); above the approver's limit approve returns APPROVAL_REQUIRED and an access approval request. handOver happens in the same transaction as approval by calling payments; confirmSent and fail mirror payments.refund.sent / payments.refund.failed. Retry is executed by payments (it checks the provider first so a refund is never sent twice). Approved never means money arrived; only sent does.

stateMachines.name: Replacement
stateMachines.notes: Replacement stock is reserved through inventory; returns.replacement.created asks orders/warehouse (Official Store) or the seller to fulfil it as a zero-charge shipment. If stock is gone, cancel with a reason and offer a refund instead. A replacement gets a new 30-day return window.

stateMachines.name: Policy version
stateMachines.notes: Baseline changes need Business Owner approval (access approval request). activate runs at effectiveFrom. Orders placed before the effective date keep their snapshot.

stateMachines.name: Category exception
stateMachines.notes: A create or change that shortens a window (approval action returns.policies.shorten-window) is saved as pending_approval with an access approval request for the Business Owner ('Send for approval'); approve and reject come from access.approval.decided. Changes that do not shorten a window skip pending_approval and are saved as scheduled. activate runs at effectiveFrom.

endpoints.summary: Issue a refund from the order page (exception refund request)

Items and amounts of one seller group, reason and funding; the dialog shows the cap from payments (GET /api/admin/payments/orders/{orderId}/refundable, in-process payments.remainingRefundable) and amounts above it return REFUND_EXCEEDS_REFUNDABLE. Creates a refund request with source exception that goes through Finance approval like any other; within the caller's limit it is approved in the same call and handed to payments. Optional trustReportId links it to a trust recommendation.
endpoints.approval: Approval action returns.refunds.approve. Within the caller's refund limit it is approved at once; above it a Finance member whose limit covers it, and a second reviewer above that limit's threshold, approve through access

integrations.purpose: Prepaid labels and QR drop-off codes; tracking events for return parcels

RETURN_NOT_ELIGIBLE.meaning: An item cannot be returned. details.items lists each item and why.

QUANTITY_EXCEEDS_RETURNABLE.meaning: More units than were delivered and not yet returned.

REMEDY_NOT_AVAILABLE.meaning: The chosen remedy is not offered (e.g. no stock for a replacement, store credit off).

REFUND_EXCEEDS_REFUNDABLE.meaning: Amount is above the remaining refundable amount. details.maxRefundable.

DUPLICATE_REFUND.meaning: An active refund already covers these items. details.refundRequestId.

SHIPPING_PAYER_NOT_ALLOWED.meaning: Platform rules do not allow the customer to pay return shipping for this reason.

RESPONSE_DEADLINE_PASSED.meaning: The respond-by time passed and Marketly is handling the return.

ESCALATION_NOT_AVAILABLE.meaning: Escalation is not open yet (seller still within the deadline). details.availableFrom.

POLICY_BELOW_BASELINE.meaning: Seller terms are less generous than the platform baseline. details.fields.

notes: Inspection: start-inspection sets the inspector (Inspecting is a sub-state of received, not a separate status). ReturnCase.inspectionChecklist is built from the order item snapshot (included items minus stated missing items), the serial number recorded at packing (warehouse.getShippedSerials, Official Store only) and inspectionChecksByCategory. Drafts (PUT /requests/{id}/inspection-draft) are cleared when the inspection or remedy is recorded. damaged_stock keeps the unit in Damaged or held without a repair or supplier route.

Evidence before a case: sellers can attach evidence to a return (POST /api/seller/returns/requests/{id}/evidence); on escalation support opens the case with returnId and copies it through returns.listEvidence.

Exports: seller return exports run through reports (registerDataset / requestExport) like every other module's exports. Returns registers dataset returns.seller.requests (seller audience; columns: return ref, order ref, item, SKU, reason, status, amount, refunded, requested at, deadline, case ref) and serves it from POST /api/seller/returns/requests/exports. Staff use POST /api/admin/reports/exports with the same rows as dataset returns.admin.requests.

Category exceptions carry applyScope (new_orders default; undelivered_orders only when nothing is shortened) and go through Business Owner approval when they shorten a window. POST /category-exceptions/preview returns the impact before saving in the same ImpactPreview shape settings uses. The preview counts open orders with orders.countOpenOrdersInCategory(categoryId, effective date) and Help articles to update with content.countHelpArticlesForPolicy('returns'); content is optional, and without it the Help line is left out.
A return is per seller: items from different sellers in one request become separate returns, each with its own RT- reference, label and decision.
Return terms are read from the order item's purchase snapshot (resolveTerms is called at checkout and stored by orders); later policy changes never apply to existing orders.
Return status and refund status are separate fields everywhere so Received or Approved is never read as money arrived.

Refund amounts are always itemised (item, discount share, shipping, return shipping deduction, other deductions with reasons) and capped by the remaining refundable amount from payments. DUPLICATE_REFUND guards against two active refunds for the same items.

Who approves money: the seller for its own returns (its earnings fund it); Finance (returns.refunds.approve, limits via access) for Official Store, platform-decided, case and exception refunds. Granting staff access to returns does not grant refund authority.
Earnings impact shown to sellers and staff comes from finance.previewRefundImpact when finance is enabled; finance books the real entries when payments.refund.sent arrives.

Stock outcomes (restock, different_condition, repair, return_to_supplier, write_off; same values as inventory) are proposed here and recorded by inventory (recordReturnOutcome), which owns the Returned stock group. Official Store parcels are scanned in by warehouse, which calls recordWarehouseReceipt.

Return labels: returns asks shipping.createLabel with kind = return and labelMethod prepaid_qr or prepaid_label (from the seller's return address or the Official Store warehouse); shipping creates the return parcel shipment, its QR code and drop-off deadline, and publishes tracking events with kind = return and returnId. Drop-off points come from shipping.findDropOffPoints. Label cost is booked by finance from returns.label.created, which knows the payer (seller, customer or platform); finance ignores kind = return in shipping.label.purchased to avoid double charging.
Official Store returns use ownerType official with sellerId null in every type, table and event (same convention as offers, orders and shipping).

Store credit refunds on returns (remedy store_credit, or a return refund request with destination store_credit) call wallet.creditRefund (phase 3) instead of payments.startRefund, idempotent per refund request id; the refund request then goes approved → sent without a card step. wallet is an optional dependency resolved at call time; while it is off store_credit is refused with REMEDY_NOT_AVAILABLE. Refunds to the original method go to payments, which returns any store-credit part of a mixed tender through wallet.creditRefund itself.
Store credit as a remedy is offered only when the wallet module (phase 3) is enabled; exchange for a different price is phase 4 (advanced returns). Same-price exchanges are phase 1.
Guests reach store endpoints with a guest session that has order access (auth/guest-orders); signed-in customers see their own returns only.
Dependency note: media and finance are optional (photos and earnings previews degrade gracefully); access is optional because approvals fall back to 'needs approval' without it.
